content.text:
## Summary

**(a) Yes — a supported, documented extension point exists.** Confirmed three independent ways:

**1. Installed source, `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev@3.18.0`** (exact version from `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/package.json`). In `bin/pwa-kit-dev.js`, the `build` command (`.command('build')` at line 274) resolves its webpack config at lines 285–291:
```js
const webpack = p.join(require.resolve('webpack'), '..', '..', '..', '.bin', 'webpack')
const projectWebpack = p.join(process.cwd(), 'webpack.config.js')
const webpackConf = fse.pathExistsSync(projectWebpack)
    ? projectWebpack
    : p.join(__dirname, '..', 'configs', 'webpack', 'config.js')
...
execSync(`${webpack} --config ${webpackConf}`, ...)
```
The identical check exists for `npm start` in `ssr/server/build-dev-server.js:133-136` (`const projectWebpackPath = path.resolve(app.options.projectDir, 'webpack.config.js'); if (fs.existsSync(projectWebpackPath)) { config = require(projectWebpackPath) }`). Both look for `webpack.config.js` at the project root and, if present, use it as the **entire** `--config` — a full replacement, not a merge. No `webpack.config.js` currently exists at this repo's root (confirmed).

**2. Origin GitHub PR** — [SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit#462](https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/pull/462) ("[V2] allow custom webpack config in projects", merged 2022-04-06) is the commit that introduced this exact mechanism: *"To add a custom webpack config, projects should add a `webpack.config.js` file in the root of their project directory... To inherit the default webpack config in your custom webpack config, insert: `const config = require('pwa-kit-build/configs/webpack/config'); module.exports = config`."*

**3. Official docs** — [Retail React App guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/retail-react-app.html): *"The Retail React App imports ready-made Webpack configurations for the client side and server side from the PWA Kit React SDK. In most cases, you don't need to change these configurations, but if you do, you can extend the Webpack configuration in `webpack.config.js`."* The [Upgrade to v2 guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/upgrade-to-v2.html) adds: *"If you haven't customized the `webpack.config.js` file... delete it... If you do have customizations, you must add them after calling the `require()` function first to get the base configuration."* (Note: `configuration-options.html` surfaced in search snippets but does **not** actually contain this content on direct fetch — don't cite it.) The require path has since been renamed from `pwa-kit-build` to `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev` — verified on disk at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/config.js`.

**(b) What using it requires.** Create root `webpack.config.js` (~10-15 lines):
```js
const configs = require('@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/config')
const client = configs.find((c) => c.name === 'client')
if (client) {
  client.optimization.splitChunks.cacheGroups.adyen = {
    test: (m) => m.context && /node_modules[\\/]@adyen[\\/]/.test(m.context),
    name: 'adyen',
    chunks: 'all',
    priority: 10 // must outrank the existing `vendor` group's implicit priority 0
  }
}
module.exports = configs
```
This is safe because `configs/webpack/config.js`'s export is a plain array of pre-built config objects (`client`/`ssr`/`renderer`/`clientOptional`/`requestProcessor`, per `config-names.js`), each passed through `SpeedMeasureWebpackPlugin.wrap()` — which returns the config **unmodified** when the `MEASURE` env var is unset (the repo's default: `disable: !process.env.MEASURE`, confirmed at `node_modules/speed-measure-webpack-plugin/index.js:91-92`). So `.name` and `.optimization` survive intact and `configs.find(c => c.name === 'client')` is reliable. No PWA-Kit-specific tradeoff is called out in the docs beyond the delete-if-unused/require-first caveat quoted above; the `priority` requirement is standard webpack `SplitChunksPlugin` behavior (not Salesforce-specific — a new cache group needs higher priority than an existing one to claim overlapping modules).

**(c) Governance flag.** No existing frozen file needs modification — `config/`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `worker/main.js`, root `package.json`, and `mobify.config.js` are all untouched; both `npm run build` and `npm start` auto-detect the new file with zero script changes required. **However, the new `webpack.config.js` itself is not listed anywhere in `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` or `protectedFiles.md`** — a real governance gap, not a resolved question. `frozenFiles.md`'s own "Build Pipeline" section already sets precedent for exactly this situation with `overrides/app/request-processor.js` ("add here when populated... it will be one of the highest-blast-radius files in the repo"). A root `webpack.config.js` controlling code-splitting for every production bundle sits in the same risk category as the Tier-1 "Runtime & Integration Config" list — recommend treating it as Integration/SI-Partner-owned by that precedent rather than waiting for the doc to catch up, and flagging this doc gap to the team before creating the file.
